Article Title: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow amid one-fifth cut to 2026 spending forecast
Article Text:
Tesla cuts 2026 capex by one fifth

SpaceX merger puts Tesla's spending under scrutiny

Revenue beats estimates, but net income plunges 43%

FSD adoption and automotive margins improve

Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent less than anticipated on capital expenditure.However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast has raised questions about its investment plans for artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and autonomous driving. The company now expects capital expenditure of around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not specify which areas would see lower spending.In the quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent a year earlier but well below the $7.5 billion analysts had expected on average, according to LSEG data.The lower spending helped Tesla report free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with market expectations of a cash outflow of $4.92 billion.Tesla's shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the results, supported by positive free cash flow, higher gross margins and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. However, the stock reversed direction to trade 2% lower. Shares have fallen around 14% this year."The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers exchange-traded funds tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon."The results come as chief executive Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX, his space venture. The unexpected cash generation could strengthen Tesla's financial position ahead of a possible deal, but lower investment in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots could raise concerns about its ability to deliver on its growth ambitions.On Tuesday, Musk described a merger between the two companies as a "good idea" and said they had formed special committees to discuss the proposal. He declined to provide further details during Wednesday's conference call with analysts.A combination would bring together businesses central to Musk's long-term vision of an integrated technology and manufacturing group spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.However, investors will want to see whether Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk's ambitions into commercial businesses, particularly as the robotaxi rollout has lagged behind his promises."The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com."The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter."Tesla's financial performance presented a mixed picture. Revenue remained flat compared with a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that had supported sales in the previous year. Nevertheless, the figure exceeded Wall Street's expectations.Net income fell 43% during the quarter.Tesla said it had ended the quarter with its largest backlog of passenger vehicles in four years. Higher petrol prices have supported demand for electric vehicles, particularly in Europe.The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, putting it on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years."Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."Tesla also reported stronger adoption of its driver-assistance technology in North America. The FSD (supervised) attach rate exceeded three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the second quarter, the company said.Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, reached 18.1% in the third quarter, above analysts' estimate of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.Tesla's energy business has recently helped offset pressures on its automotive operations. The latter remain under scrutiny as competitors worldwide launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla continues to rely heavily on its ageing Model 3 and Model Y.Despite the competitive pressures, Tesla aims to produce five million vehicles annually by around 2030, compared with an expected 2.5 million this year.
Article Summary: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow, beating Wall Street's expectations. Company cuts 2026 capex forecast by one fifth to $20 billion, down from $25 billion. Results come as CEO Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX.

Article Title: Rupee under pressure: Currency slips to 94.50 as oil rises, Dalal Street struggles in red
Article Text:
Rupee gives up some gains

NEW DELHI: Rupee weakened in early trade on Thursday, losing 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar as rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall.The currency opened at 94.47 at the interbank foreign exchange market before slipping to 94.50. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the dollar on Wednesday.Forex analysts said the rupee was trading on a flat-to-lower note amid pressure from the domestic stock market and higher oil prices. The dollar’s weakness and easing US Treasury yields offered some support to the currency.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, expects rupee to retain a slight positive bias."We expect the rupee to trade with a slight positive bias on IPO related foreign inflows and weakness in the dollar. Softening of US treasury yields and reports that Russia is ready for new peace talks may also support the rupee," he told PTI.Choudhary added that market participants would track the weekly unemployment claims data from the US for further direction.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.21 per cent to 101.56. In contrast, Brent crude futures rose 1.58 per cent to $110.54 per barrel.Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak NEO, said the rupee remained finely balanced within the 94-97 range."The RBI has bought itself time, the Jio IPO has added near-term dollar supply, and a US trade agreement could strengthen the structural inflow story. But if portfolio selling accelerates again or crude makes a decisive move towards $120, that balance will be tested," Banerjee added.The domestic equity market also remained under pressure during early trade. BSE Sensex dropped 642.51 points to 73,067.18, while NSE Nifty50 declined 241.35 points to 22,570.90.Despite the weakness in equities on Thursday morning, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers in the previous session. They purchased equities worth Rs 1,022.32 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee loses 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday. Rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise against the dollar.

Article Title: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia raise concerns over oil supplies
Article Text:
Crude prices hold above $110 per barrel

Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of Hormuz

US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks rise

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.The threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.US crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy backed the proposed talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%. US state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region. Latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday.

Article Title: Jio IPO subscribed over 5x as institutions bid big
Article Text:
The retail portion of the offer—that was subscribed 70% on Day 1—was also fully subscribed on Thursday

MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, through which the company is raising Rs 30,213 crore, making it the largest such offer in India, was subscribed over five times at the close of bidding on Day 2. Institutional investors continued to lead the bidding process—that had helped the IPO to get fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening on Day 1—with high-net-worth investors (HNIs) following closely, data from the bourses showed.The retail portion of the offer—that was subscribed 70% on Day 1—was also fully subscribed on Thursday, with the Day 2 closing data showing 1.5 times subscription for 8.5 crore shares that are on offer.At the close of Day 2, the total demand for Jio shares was worth about Rs 3.7 lakh crore, including the anchor portion. On Thursday, the institutional (QIB) part of the IPO, in which a little over 4.9 crore shares were offered, was subscribed nearly 13.3 times, while the HNI portion, in which about 3.6 crore shares were reserved, was subscribed six times. Usually, in most IPOs, institutional players apply on the last day of the offer.Exchange data also showed that the portion reserved for employees was subscribed over two times while the part reserved for RIL shareholders was subscribed a little over four times.In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,360, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of Rs 241 over the upper limit of the IPO price band. The current GMP is slightly lower than Rs 273, the highest level seen a day before the IPO opened, but much higher than the opening quote of Rs 148 on Oct 4, quotes from websites tracking the trend in the unofficial market for shares showed. The strong response to the IPO comes on the back of a Rs 2.5 lakh-crore anchor book that was subscribed 30 times the size, which was Rs 8,110 crore, disclosures showed.
Article Summary: The retail portion of the offer was also fully subscribed on Thursday. At the close of Day 2, the total demand for Jio shares was worth about Rs 3.7 lakh crore. The strong response to the IPO comes on the back of a Rs 2.5 lakh-crore anchor book.

Article Title: Yes Bank Additional Tier 1 bondholders seek interest payment
Article Text:
According to analysts, revisiting past coupons raises legal and accounting issues.

MUMBAI: Retail bondholders of YES Bank have asked Axis Trustee Services, the debenture trustee, to secure payment of overdue coupons (interest payments) on the bank’s Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds, restore their holdings in demat accounts and seek regulatory intervention, days after Supreme Court dismissed appeals against Bombay high court’s ruling that quashed the March 2020 write-off.The YES Bank AT1 Retail Bond Holders Association cited Companies Act and Sebi obligations in seeking an explanation for non-payment of the 9% bond coupon due Oct 18, three days after the Oct 15 court order restoring the bonds. It also demanded payment of coupons skipped in 2020-25 and arrangements for the forthcoming Dec 23 coupon on 9.5% bonds.According to analysts, revisiting past coupons raises legal and accounting issues. The write-off was recognised in profit and loss, so restoring the bonds could affect past profits. Coupon payments on high-risk AT1 bonds are also contingent on the bank’s financial performance.The association asked Axis Trustee to disclose YES Bank’s position on each missed coupon, cancellation notices and correspondence since March 2020, including any reliance on contractual discretion or record dates. It also sought coordination with the bank, registrars NSDL and CDSL in order to restore demat holdings.Citing the apex court’s observations that AT1 bonds are high-risk instruments meant for institutional investors, despite YES Bank selling them to individuals, the association sought intervention by RBI and markets regulator Sebi.
Article Summary: YES Bank AT1 Retail Bond Holders Association cited Companies Act and Sebi obligations. It also demanded payment of coupons skipped in 2020-25 and arrangements for the forthcoming Dec 23 coupon on 9.5% bonds. The write-off was recognised in profit and loss, so restoring the bonds could affect past profits.

Article Title: Jio Platforms' IPO becomes first public offer globally to cross 1 crore applications: Report
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Jio Platforms’ initial public offering (IPO) has become the first public issue globally to receive more than one crore applications, news agency PTI reported citing sources on Friday, as investor demand surged on the final day of bidding.The $3.2 billion offering by billionaire Mukesh Ambani ’s telecom and digital services company has attracted strong interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and shareholders. The IPO, the largest in India’s history, is being closely watched as a test of investor appetite for large listings amid increased scrutiny of artificial intelligence-linked stocks.Subscriptions crossed six times the shares on offer by Friday. Assuming bids were largely placed at the upper end of the price band of Rs 1,119, total demand exceeded $14.5 billion, according to Reuters.The strong response follows substantial demand from anchor investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity. The $854 million worth of shares reserved for these investors received bids exceeding $25 billion on Monday.Jio Platforms’ IPO opened on Wednesday and was fully subscribed within two hours, an unusually rapid start for an Indian public issue.In most Indian IPOs, subscription levels typically build gradually, with institutional investors often placing bids closer to the deadline.The IPO values Jio Platforms at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India’s largest companies by market capitalisation when trading begins on October 28.The company operates a mobile network serving more than 500 million users and has Meta Platforms and Alphabet’s Google among its investors. It is led by Akash Ambani, the eldest son of Mukesh Ambani.Jio Platforms is part of Reliance Industries, which is often viewed by Indian investors as a long-term wealth creator. Reliance shares have delivered returns of around 900% since 2006, outperforming the benchmark Nifty index’s 685% return over the same period, according to LSEG data.
Article Summary: The $3.2 billion offering by Mukesh Ambani ’s telecom and digital services company has attracted strong interest from institutional and retail investors. The IPO, the largest in India’s history, is being closely watched as a test of investor appetite for large listings.

Article Title: Crude rises, rupee falls & Dalal Street trips again
Article Text:
At $120/BBL, Indian Crude Basket’s Oct Avg Price Hits 14-Yr High

This came on the back of talks of escalation of the war between US and Iran in the Persian Gulf region.

MUMBAI: Rising crude oil prices with the Indian crude basket at a 14-year high, fresh weakness of the rupee after an eight-session gain and sliding Asian markets weighed on investor sentiment on Dalal Street on Thursday.As a result, sensex showed a weak trend from the start of the session and closed 460 points or 0.6% lower at 73,249 points. On NSE, Nifty lost 124 points or 0.5% to close at 22,688 points.On Thursday, the average price for the Indian crude basket for Oct hit a high of $120 per barrel, up from the recent high of $114.5 in April. This is the highest level since it hit $123.6 in March 2012, data from Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell of ministry of petroleum & natural gas showed. The Indian crude basket is a derived basket of two types of crude oil, Brent and Oman & Dubai, that are imported by Indian refiners.This jump in the Indian basket came as Brent crude prices shot up to over the $112 per-barrel mark, the highest level seen since May this year. This came on the back of talks of escalation of the war between US and Iran in the Persian Gulf region.Shooting oil prices also weakened the rupee that, after an eight-session rally, reversed trend to hover close to the 95/$ level, having fallen 36 paise.Weakness across major Asian markets also made Indian investors nervous, market players said.According to Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth, India market’s downward spiral continued due to external factors as a fresh escalation in the West Asia conflict pushed oil prices up. “Weak Asian and European market cues and a steep fall in the rupee against the dollar further (affected investor) sentiment,” Punj wrote in a note. “While (corporate) earnings have been a mixed bag so far, concerns over an uptick in inflation due to higher crude oil prices and persistent (foreign fund) selling in local shares could further drive investors to safe haven dollar assets. ”Among the major Asian market indices, Kospi in Korea closed 3.5% down, Hang Seng in Hong Kong closed 3% down, Nikkei in Japan was down 2.7% at the close while Shanghai Composite in China closed 1.5% lower. European markets too were mostly in the red in late trades with CAC 40 in France down 1.4%, DAX in Germany down 1.1% and FTSE 100 down 0.3%.In the domestic market, foreign investors again led the selling, after recording a net buying figure on Wednesday. At the close of Thursday’s session, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net sellers at Rs 3,459 crore while domestic funds were net buyers at Rs 2,891 crore, provisional data on BSE showed. The day’s session left investors poorer by about Rs 3.3 lakh crore.
Article Summary: The average price for the Indian crude basket for Oct hit a high of $120 per barrel. This is the highest level since it hit $123.6 in March 2012. Brent crude prices shot up to over the $112 per-barrel mark.

Article Title: Videos, the new gateway reshaping online retail
Article Text:
Live Commerce, Interesting Clips Scale ToCreate Content-To-Commerce Ecosystem.

For one, there’s live commerce wherein creators showcase a product or give demonstrations in real time.

Cos’ video strategy

MUMBAI: Indians are no longer just shopping; they are video-shopping. Videos drive a lot of traction on online platforms such as Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Meesho. Consumers scroll through creator-led content reels or shorts, discovering a host of new brands and products with many eventually clicking on the ‘buy’ tab, often embedded in them. The trend is more popular among Gen Z shoppers and consumers residing in smaller towns, companies said.For one, there’s live commerce wherein creators showcase a product or give demonstrations in real time. The other format is shortform shoppable videos which may or may not always feature creators and may not be live, but they allow people to buy products without leaving the video stream by way of links included within them. Live commerce and shoppable videos have both scaled to collectively create a content-to-commerce ecosystem. For Bengaluru-based IT professional Sanjeet Singh, influencer reels play a big role in product discovery. “Reels give me an idea of what the product is,” Singh said.Social media platforms such as Instagram and YouTube had already made access easier than ever—people sat at their homes, browsed through videos, subscribing to influencer-led recommendations and buying products.Platforms took note of the shopping habit and launched their own video and live formats.Amazon, for instance, launched Live in 2022 while players such as Myntra and Meesho joined in after a couple of years or so. The strategy seemed to have worked—creator-led discovery has influenced the shopping journeys of nearly two crore consumers on Amazon so far in 2026 while for Meesho, active order-generating content grew by over 140% to 1.7 million in Q1FY27, the firms said.Besides, all the e-commerce companies have active accounts on platforms such as Instagram wherein they collaborate with influencers to market their products and sale events, amplifying visibility.Creator-led commerce will become a key driver for e-commerce growth, contributing nearly $25 billion in gross merchandise value (GMV) by 2030, a joint April study by Deloitte and Google showed. “Creator content will scale significantly, with creator-owned storefronts and online videos becoming instantly shoppable. Eventually, these formats will also help onboard 50-60 million new online shoppers from tier 2 markets by effectively addressing key barriers around trust, product understanding, and quality,” analysts said in the report.Amazon has scaled Live beyond real-time product demonstrations and creator recommendations to shortform, shoppable video experiences that are integrated directly into the shopping journey. “Short-form shopping videos complement live commerce and help keep product discovery contextual and engaging. The video format helps customers understand how a product works, see it in a real-life context, compare options, ask questions and move directly towards purchase,” said Nidhi Thakkar, head of social commerce, emerging countries at Amazon.Nearly 70% of creator-led purchases on Amazon marketplace have come from non-metro cities, including cities such as Bathinda, Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore and Dehradun. “This reflects the role regional creators are playing in helping customers discover products through content that is relevant to their language, context and communities,” Thakkar added.Myntra launched Ultimate Glam Clan (UGC) in Aug 2024—a shopper creator programme which enables customers to create fashion and beauty content around products they discover and shop on the platform. UGC grew to more than eight million sign-ups and 12 million cumulative pieces of content as of Sept 2026, the company claimed.It also built Glamstream in July 2025, which brings together creator-led video, entertainment and commerce within the Myntra app. “Video is increasingly becoming an important part of the discovery journey, helping consumers explore fashion and beauty through creator recommendations, styling inspiration and realworld context. Users engaging with social commerce content convert around 10% better than those who do not, highlighting the role of content in influencing purchase decisions,” said Deepash Jain, vice-president, marketing, Myntra, adding that the format has enabled platforms to move beyond traditional catalogue-led shopping.Flipkart’s video commerce ecosystem spans shortform videos, live shopping, creator-led product demos, Q&As, gamified formats and seamless in-video shopping journeys. “Shopping in India is increasingly being shaped by what consumers watch, share and trust,” said Ramesh Gururaja, senior vice president, consumer products and growth, FCC, Ads and Cleartrip at Flipkart.
Article Summary: Videos drive a lot of traction on online platforms such as Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Meesho. The trend is more popular among Gen Z shoppers and consumers residing in smaller towns. Live commerce and shoppable videos have both scaled to collectively create a content-to-commerce ecosystem.

Article Title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS business, shares tank
Article Text:
Investors were bearish on the eMudhra stock after the cyber incident.

BENGALURU: Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day on Thursday after it announced its decision to exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.The company’s board decided to withdraw from the business after reviewing its commercial prospects and the scrutiny triggered by the incident. The global SSL/TLS business contributes about 1% of eMudhra’s revenue, but rising compliance requirements, increasing costs and competition from free certificate providers have reduced its potential returns, the company said.“The scrutiny was disproportionate to the revenue contribution of the business,” Kaushik Srinivasan, co-founder of eMudhra, told TOI, explaining the board’s decision. He said the board met on Thursday to assess the business’s future following the incident and the sharp fall in the company’s share price over the past two sessions.Investors were bearish on the eMudhra stock after the cyber incident. In two sessions since the incident, its stock price has crashed 36% to Rs 345 by Thursday’s close, from Rs 539 at Monday’s close.The issue was reported on Oct 17 by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team, who flagged weaknesses in the keys associated with the eight eMudhra intermediate certificates.Srinivasan said the economics of the business were becoming less attractive as certificate validity periods shortened. “The return on investment, considering the effort, investment and compliance requirements, is becoming less attractive. It makes more sense to strengthen and invest in our enterprise solutions business, which has higher margins and greater potential,” he said.
Article Summary: Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day on Thursday. The company announced its decision to exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.

Article Title: 'Your funds are safe with us': SBI's message to customers after major data breach
Article Text:
SBI informs customers affected by data breach, says account balances and funds are safe

NEW DELHI: State Bank of India (SBI) has informed customers whose data was identified in a recent breach, saying their account balances and funds remain safe."Further to our earlier post regarding the recent cyber incident, the Bank has individually informed all customers whose data was identified as being involved through email and/or WhatsApp. We reiterate that your account balances and funds are safe with us," the bank said in a statement on Friday.The update comes a day after SBI confirmed that a preliminary analysis had identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information among around 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web.The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and appointed an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on October 16.The records identified in the preliminary analysis reportedly contained customers’ names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch details, customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records.The disclosure followed a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI.The post claimed the dataset contained 3.75 lakh rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.SBI has said a detailed investigation is required to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the potential risks to customers and the bank.The bank has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to conduct an independent assessment. It has also said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally.The investigation is underway, with remedial and preventive measures being implemented.
Article Summary: State Bank of India (SBI) has informed customers whose data was identified in a recent breach, saying their account balances and funds remain safe. The update comes a day after SBI confirmed that a preliminary analysis had identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information among around 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web.

Article Title: Starting a food business? FSSAI offers help to navigate safety rules and approvals
Article Text:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India will operationalise a Start-Up Cell next month.

NEW DELHI: For entrepreneurs launching food businesses, navigating food safety regulations can be as challenging as developing a product. From securing licences to getting labelling and product claims right, gaps in regulatory understanding can lead to avoidable errors and delays.To address these challenges, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) will operationalise a dedicated Start-Up Cell next month officials said. The cell will help emerging food businesses understand regulatory requirements and seek guidance on compliance.According to an FSSAI social media post, start-ups can approach the cell every Wednesday during a dedicated online session to get their queries addressed. They can also email questions to startupcell@fssai.gov.in.The cell will provide guidance on food business licensing and registration, product standards and categorisation, approvals, labelling and advertising claims, testing, imports, e-commerce compliance, novel foods and nutraceuticals.These are areas where regulatory clarity can be particularly important for new businesses seeking to bring products to market while meeting food safety requirements.However, the cell will offer advisory guidance, not exemptions from existing rules or automatic approvals. Licensing, approval and enforcement decisions will remain with the competent authorities. Queries requiring legal interpretation will be vetted by FSSAI’s Legal Division.The authority said information shared for query resolution would be handled confidentially and anonymised for policy analysis. The cell will also provide a channel for start-ups to flag recurring regulatory challenges and seek information about FSSAI initiatives and guidance materials.For entrepreneurs, the initiative could offer a single point of contact for understanding applicable food safety requirements before products reach consumers. FSSAI has not specified in its post how start-ups can register for the weekly sessions or when the cell will become operational.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India will operationalise a dedicated Start-Up Cell next month. The cell will help emerging food businesses understand regulatory requirements and seek guidance on compliance. Start-ups can approach the cell every Wednesday during a dedicated online session to get their queries addressed.

Article Title: At €310 billion, Union minister Piyush Goyal eyes 10x rise in Indo-German trade
Article Text:
Goyal said the FTA could be signed by Dec and implemented within four to five months.

BERLIN: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Thursday set an ambitious target of increasing bilateral trade with Germany tenfold to 310 billion euros, urging businesses to forge partnerships ahead of implementation of the India-EU free trade agreement (FTA).At the inauguration of the India Centre and Indo-German Business Forum in Berlin, Goyal said the FTA could be signed by Dec and implemented within four to five months. “We had 31.5 billion euros (in 2025) and (if) we were to be able to add a zero to that, make it 310 billion euros. How would that sound? Now, we can certainly make that happen,” he said, emphasising the need to draw up concrete plans to realise the ambition.Goyal is on a visit to Germany and the Netherlands from Oct 22 to 27, leading a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups to explore opportunities in trade, investment and industrial cooperation. The minister said Germany’s precision engineering and commitment to quality complemented India’s infrastructure expansion, digital capabilities and young, skilled workforce, creating scope for collaboration in manufacturing, technology and supply chains. He said the two countries had little to compete with each other and could together strengthen supply chain resilience and have a transformational impact on each other’s economies.He asked businesses to start identifying customers and investors, exploring partnerships and aligning product quality and pricing with market requirements rather than wait for the FTA to come into effect. “This is the time partnerships need to be forged. This is the time connects need to be made with potential customers, collaborators, investors,” Goyal said, adding that companies must prepare to “trade, invest smarter, faster and get the best out of this agreement”.Negotiations for the India-EU FTA concluded in Jan this year following talks between PM Narendra Modi and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Goyal said the agreement had received unanimous support from all 27 EU member states and expressed confidence that the remaining process would move rapidly. India-EU trade stood at 118 billion euros in 2025.Goyal outlined priorities for India and Germany, including strengthening economic security, creating industrial opportunities through the green transition and advancing emerging technologies. He called for closer cooperation in apprenticeships and skilling, areas in which Germany has considerable expertise.Germany’s minister for economic affairs and energy, Katherina Reiche, said bilateral trade remained below potential, with India not featuring among Germany’s top 20 trading partners despite goods trade worth around 31 billion euros in 2025.“We could at least double the trade amount we have right now,” she said, calling for greater investment and industrial partnerships. Reiche said German companies had an investment stock of over 28 billion euros in India and that the proposed German-Indian CEO forum was expected to bring business leaders together and encourage fresh investments.Speaking at Berlin Global Dialogue, Goyal said the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) could hurt European industries. “If you put a CBAM on yourself and put a 50% import duty to bring steel into your country, you are inviting disaster. Your cost of living will go up, your people will be unhappy, your industry will be outpriced.”
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal set an ambitious target of increasing bilateral trade with Germany tenfold to 310 billion euros. He urged businesses to forge partnerships ahead of implementation of the India-EU free trade agreement. Goyal is on a visit to Germany and the Netherlands from Oct 22 to 27.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags critical vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications

Bengaluru:

It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems. Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security. “Approximately 75% of all internet runs on PHP or some framework based on PHP including Wordpress, Drupal, Laravel, Joomla and these vulnerabilities impact the default configuration of the same. It allows a Threat Actor to achieve remote code execution trivially. This will allow bad actors to get access to your server,” said Anirudh Batra, threat researcher in Bengaluru-based cybersecurity firm CloudSEK.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”

Article Title: Ultraviolette eyes Europe expansion with Venom launch
Article Text:
Bengaluru:

(With inputs from agencies)

Ultraviolette on Thursday launched its X-47 Venom electric motorcycle as it prepares to expand its European presence and increase monthly motorcycle sales from around 700 to 1,000 in the first quarter of 2027.The Bengaluru-based company will introduce the Venom in Europe on Nov 3 at the EICMA motorcycle exhibition in Milan. It already exports to 20 European countries, including Germany, France, Italy and the UK. Europe accounts for roughly 10% of its current sales, the company said.The Venom is priced at Rs 2.6 lakh, ex-showroom Bengaluru, for the first 5,000 customers. The starting price will rise to Rs 3 lakh thereafter. Bookings opened on Thursday. The model is an updated version of the X-47 Crossover.The launch comes as Ultraviolette broadens its product portfolio, expands its distribution network and adds manufacturing capacity. Beyond Europe, it plans to enter the US in 2027 and is exploring opportunities in Latin America and Southeast Asia.Domestic expansion will accompany the overseas push. CEO and co-founder Narayan Subramaniam told reporters on Thursday that the company plans to expand its retail network from around 50 locations to 100 by the first quarter of 2027.With additional products, including the Shockwave motorcycle and Tesseract scooter, it is targeting sales of around 10,000 vehicles a month by this time next year.This broader target goes beyond the near-term increase expected from its motorcycle business as the company prepares to enter the electric scooter market. The planned additions will expand its portfolio across sports, crossover and street-and-dirt motorcycles, as well as scooters.Ultraviolette raised $85 million in September in a funding round led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures, with participation from Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan. The funds are intended to support manufacturing capacity, new electric vehicle platforms and international expansion.The company has also announced plans to invest Rs 779 crore over five years in a new factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The facility is designed to ramp up to an annual capacity of 2.5 lakh vehicles in phases. It will manufacture the Tesseract scooter and future products, alongside the company’s existing Bengaluru operations.The Venom is the first motorcycle built on Ultraviolette’s VX-100 platform, which combines new battery, motor and control systems. The architecture can accommodate different battery capacities and power outputs, allowing the company to extend it across future models and markets.Subramaniam described VX-100 as establishing “a technology foundation for a new generation of products across segments and markets”. The company developed the platform as it prepared to expand beyond its existing motorcycle portfolio.Founded in 2016 by Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette counts TVS Motor, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho and Lingotto among its investors. Its existing motorcycle portfolio includes the F77 range and X-47 Crossover.
Article Summary: Bengaluru-based company will introduce the Venom in Europe on Nov 3 at the EICMA motorcycle exhibition in Milan. The Venom is priced at Rs 2.6 lakh, ex-showroom Bengaluru, for the first 5,000 customers. The starting price will rise to Rs 3 lakh thereafter.

Article Title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS biz as shares; 30,000 certificates affected
Article Text:
Bengaluru:

Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day on Thursday after the company announced its decision to voluntarily exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.The company’s board decided to withdraw from the business after reviewing its commercial prospects and the scrutiny triggered by the incident. The global SSL/TLS business contributes about 1% of eMudhra’s revenue, but rising compliance requirements, increasing costs and competition from free certificate providers have reduced its potential returns, the company said.“The scrutiny was disproportionate to the revenue contribution of the business,” Kaushik Srinivasan, co-founder of eMudhra, told TOI, explaining the board’s decision. He said the board met on Thursday to assess the business’s future following the incident and the sharp fall in the company’s share price over the past two sessions.Investors were bearish on the eMudhra stock after the cyber incident. In two sessions since the incident, its stock price has crashed 36% to Rs 345 by Thursday’s close, from Rs 539 at Monday’s close.The issue was reported on Oct 17 by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team, who flagged weaknesses in the keys associated with the eight eMudhra intermediate certificates.Srinivasan said the economics of the business were becoming less attractive as certificate validity periods shortened. “The return on investment, considering the effort, investment and compliance requirements, is becoming less attractive. It makes more sense to strengthen and invest in our enterprise solutions business, which has higher margins and greater potential,” he said.The incident stems from a key-generation process conducted on April 30, 2025. Srinivasan said delays in procuring hardware for North American operations meant the company had to generate keys in India and subsequently export them. A script error resulted in weak keys, while inadequate maker-checker controls contributed to the problem.“It was a script error and human error,” he said, adding that the company would strengthen operational and security controls and review its processes.The company said it revoked the affected intermediate certificate authorities within 14 hours of discovering the issue and disclosed it promptly. Chairman V Srinivasan said the incident did not involve a compromise of the company’s infrastructure or a data breach, and that physical and logical security controls remained intact.The incident has also affected customers relying on eMudhra’s G3 root, a top-level certificate authority that helps browsers establish trust in digital certificates used to authenticate websites and secure connections.Kaushik Srinivasan said around 30,000 certificates associated with the G3 root were affected after it was distrusted, and the company was working to transition them. One customer in North America was impacted, he said.The company is working with browser programmes and customers to manage the transition. It plans to replace affected certificates and use alternative providers where required, while seeking to minimise disruption to customer-facing services.“Our G1 root, as I understand it, continues to be trusted,” Srinivasan said, adding that the company was also working to transition customers covered by the G1 root. The company has said its G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until the transition is complete and that replacement certificates will be provided free of cost through partners.Srinivasan said the company would commission an independent review by an empanelled auditor to examine its cryptographic keys, key inventories and key-generation processes. The findings will be made public, he said.eMudhra plans to focus on its other businesses, including digital signature certificates, eSign, enterprise public key infrastructure platforms, its emSigner eSignature Suite, and identity and authentication solutions. The company said these operations run on infrastructure separate from its global SSL/TLS business and remain unaffected.While the direct revenue contribution from SSL/TLS is small, Srinivasan said the company was also seeking to contain the reputational risk arising from the incident and restore customer confidence.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), in an advisory issued on Wednesday, said eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities were affected by a key-generation flaw that resulted in weak cryptographic private keys.
Article Summary: Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day. The company announced its decision to voluntarily exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.

transition from temporary assignment to local employment; or

movement from a conventional expatriate arrangement to a recurring hybrid-working pattern.

Ongoing assignments as on 15 July 2026 –

Welcome step forward, but careful implementation is key

(The author, Ravi Jain is Tax Partner at Vialto. Vikas Kumar, Director, and Pawan Digga, Manager at Vialto, have also contributed to this article. Views are personal. Note: This article is intended as a general explanation of the new arrangements and not as tax, immigration, employment-law or social-security advice for a particular employee or assignment.)

Employees movement from one country to another for work usually brings questions around the minimum salary, immigration and taxes. Such moves can also trigger less obvious social security obligations in both countries, potentially increasing the cost of an international assignment. This was a particular concern for employees moving between India and the UK.Historically, the two countries did not have a bilateral social security agreement as against the other European countries with whom India has a Social Security Agreement (SSA) i.e. Belgium, Germany, France, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Denmark, Finland, Luxembourg, Portugal and Sweden.Therefore, an employee temporarily sent from India to the UK could, subject to conditions, remain outside the UK National Insurance Contributions (UK NICs) for up to 52 weeks as per the UK social security laws. However, once this period ended, UK contributions could become relevant even where contributions continued in India.The position could be even more immediate for employees moving from the UK to India, who could fall within India's social security regime as International Workers (IWs) from the start of their assignment. In practical terms, an international assignment could therefore result in social security contributions becoming payable in both countries.Against this backdrop, social security became an important part of the broader India-UK economic trade discussions. The two governments ultimately concluded a Double Contributions Convention (DCC) to provide a framework for determining social security contribution obligations for eligible employees moving between the two countries. The DCC, which came into force on 15 July 2026, is intended to address the risk of double social security contributions on qualifying international assignments. Here are the key features of this Agreement alongside practical issues which require clarifications.The basic rule: pay social security in one countryThe agreement is designed so that an employee is generally subject to one country's legislation (UK/India). A qualifying employee may continue under the home country's social-security system where he/she:Put simply, an employee sent from India to work temporarily in the UK for up to five years can, if the conditions are fulfilled, remain subject to Indian social security instead of paying UK NICs. Conversely, a qualifying employee sent from the UK to India can remain subject to UK social-security legislation and continue paying UK NICs rather than Indian social-security contribution. This is a major practical simplification for international mobile employees and their employers.UK-to-India assignments: Social security position before and after the DCCAs per the UK tax and social security authorities (HMRC), to get the benefit of detachment (i.e. relief from double contribution) under the Agreement, the employee must already have been covered by the social security system of his home country before the assignment starts. The employee and employer must have paid, or be treated as having paid, contributions for at least 30 days before the employee leaves the home country, or for the calendar month before the temporary assignment begins.This makes pre-departure planning particularly important. HR and global mobility teams should check the employee's social security status before the assignment starts rather than trying to resolve the position after the employee has already moved.The Certificate of Coverage (COC) becomes an important document under the new framework. In practical terms, it provides evidence that an employee remains covered by the social security system of the home country while temporarily working in the other country. An employee who remains covered under India's social security system while working in the UK should obtain a COC from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). This provides evidence that Indian social security contributions continue to apply and that UK NICs are not due under the DCC. Similarly, an employee remaining within UK social security while working in India, may apply to HMRC for a UK COC using Form CA9107.Employers should therefore make the COC process part of their standard pre-departure checklist, alongside immigration, payroll and tax requirements. The EPFO has also updated its online portal to facilitate COC applications for eligible employees under the India-UK DCC.This distinction deserves emphasis. The DCC determines where social-security contributions are paid. It does not itself confer a right to enter, stay or work in the other country. The UK Government's DCC explainer specifically says that nothing in the arrangement changes the UK's immigration regime or its ability to control its borders.An employee still needs to satisfy the applicable immigration requirements to work in the UK. Therefore, social-security coverage and immigration permission are two separate compliance requirements.An employee could potentially satisfy the DCC conditions for social-security purposes but still needs an appropriate Visa and sponsorship arrangements to perform the proposed work in the host country.An assignment that is extended after it begins does not automatically lose protection under the DCC. For example, if an employee is sent from London to Mumbai for three years and the project is later extended to five and a half years, the employee may remain covered by the UK social security system until the assignment ends or the 60-month limit is reached, whichever is earlier.HMRC illustrates this with a UK employee who’s planned 24-month assignment is extended to 66 months and clarifies that UK legislation continues to apply for the first 60 months, after which Indian social security legislation applies.The DCC includes an anti-reset rule to prevent employers or employees from repeatedly starting fresh assignments to extend home-country social security coverage within the overall period of 60 months. Generally, once a detached-worker assignment ends, the employee must wait six months before a new qualifying assignment can begin. If the earlier assignment lasted less than six months, the required waiting period is equal to the length of that assignment.Reflecting the growth of cross-border remote working, the Agreement may also cover employees who temporarily choose to work from the other country for personal reasons, provided their employer agrees and the other prescribed conditions are met. HMRC’s guidance illustrates this with employees who temporarily work overseas to join a partner or to be closer to elderly family members.In such cases, the employee may qualify as a ‘detached worker’ (i.e. eligible for benefit under the Agreement) and remain covered by the social security system of the home country. This flexibility is particularly relevant for multinational employers developing cross-border remote-working policies.Special transitional rules apply to employees who were already on assignment when the DCC came into force on 15 July 2026. HMRC’s guidance clarifies that such employees do not automatically qualify as ‘detached workers’ (i.e. eligible for benefit under the Agreement). For example, an employee of an Indian employer who was working in the UK immediately before that date (15 July 2026) under the existing 52-week period, NIC exemption became subject to UK social security legislation from 15 July 2026, rather than receiving a new 60-month exemption under the DCC. A corresponding principle applies to relevant UK employees who were already working in India. This distinction between assignments already underway and those beginning on or after 15 July 2026 is therefore particularly important for employers’ global mobility and payroll teams.The position is more complex for employees who normally divide their work between India and the UK, as the DCC does not provide a special rule for this working pattern. However, HMRC clarifies that in such cases, UK NICs shall be payable on earnings from work performed in the UK and Indian social security contribution being payable on earnings from work performed in India. This differs significantly from a straightforward temporary assignment covered by the 60-month detached-worker rule. As international hybrid-working arrangements become more common, employers will therefore need to review each arrangement carefully rather than assume that the five-year rule removes every cross-border social security obligation.The benefits of the DCC should also be considered alongside its limitations. First, it is fundamentally a contributions coordination agreement, not a comprehensive social security benefits agreement. The UK Government expressly explains that the DCC does not govern access to benefits such as the UK State Pension or change the rules determining access to benefits. Second, this Agreement does not apply to self-employment cases. Third, the Agreement itself does not change immigration rules. Employers should therefore treat social security, personal taxation, payroll, immigration and employment law as independent compliance matters. An exemption under one regime does not automatically settle the others.The DCC and HMRC’s guidance explain the core contribution rules, but additional practical guidance from HMRC, the EPFO and other relevant Indian authorities would help employers apply them consistently. Official FAQs with illustrations would be useful, especially on the following issues.HMRC clearly recognises employer-approved personal-choice remote working to qualify as detached worker. Some practical instances would be particularly useful for employees whose arrangements sit between traditional detachment and regular two-country working. For example, how should an employer analyse an employee who ordinarily works in India but is permitted to work from the UK for several weeks every quarter? How should the position differ where that pattern is agreed in advance for several years?There is lack of clarity on the “wage” on which Indian social security contributions should be calculated while an Indian employee is detached to the UK. For Indian employees temporarily assigned to the UK, it is provided that employee and employer contributions in India are to be calculated on the total wages, determined under the Indian social security legislation. This raises an important practical question for payroll teams, particularly where contributions before the assignment were based on the statutory wage ceiling (i.e. at INR 25,000 per month) or on employee’s basic salary and not on total wages. A clear guidance on the applicable contribution base that should apply while a COC is in force and whether, on the employee’s return to India, such base may revert to the basis that applied before the UK assignment. Specific examples covering different categories of employees and establishments would help employers apply the provision consistently and plan their costs.What happens when the factual assumptions supporting the original COC change. Common examples include:These situations should not automatically be treated as continuing to qualify merely because the original COC covered a period of up to 60 months. In practice, employers may need to reassess whether the conditions supporting the original coverage continue to be satisfied. A clarification from authorities will help accordingly.The agreement provides that the ongoing assignments as on 15 July 2026 shall not be covered. But that leaves practical questions for employers seeking to reorganise legitimate assignments.For example, can an existing assignment formally end and a genuinely new assignment subsequently begin? If so, what conditions must be satisfied before that new assignment can qualify for benefit under the Agreement? How should short-term assignments (upto 1 year period) that were still within the 52-week domestic-law exemption be handled? These are precisely the situations in which coordinated FAQs and worked examples from HMRC, EPFO and the relevant authorities would give employers much-needed certainty.The DCC is a significant step forward for employee mobility between India and the UK, as it provides a clear framework for determining where social security contributions are payable during a qualifying temporary assignment. Its benefit should not, however, be described as a blanket five-year exemption: eligible detached workers remain covered by one country’s social security system, subject to the conditions of the Agreement, rather than being exempt from contributions altogether.Employers should therefore assess eligibility before departure, obtain and maintain the appropriate COC, and review the position whenever assignment terms or working arrangements change. With sound planning and further administrative guidance, the DCC should reduce double-contribution costs, improve compliance certainty and make cross-border talent deployment between the two countries more efficient.
Article Summary: The DCC determines where social-security contributions are paid. The agreement is designed so that an employee is generally subject to one country's legislation. An employee temporarily sent from India to the UK could, subject to conditions, remain outside the UK National Insurance Contributions (UK NICs) for up to 52 weeks.

Article Title: India’s private capex pipeline rises 39% to Rs 99.7 lakh crore, UBI flags risks
Article Text:
India’s private capex pipeline rises 39% to Rs 99.7 lakh crore, UBI flags risks

Two sectors account for most of the increase

Five states dominate investment growth

Power investment gap raises execution concerns

India’s planned private sector investments touched Rs 99.7 lakh crore in September 2026, with the pipeline expanding 39% over a year. However, the sharp rise in project costs has not been matched by a similar increase in the number of projects, raising concerns about how widely the investment recovery is spread across the economy, according to a report by Union Bank of India (UBI) Research.The pipeline has grown 87% in two years, but the number of projects has increased by only 18%. This suggests that larger projects, rather than a broad increase in investment activity, have accounted for much of the growth.The report said, “The capex cycle is firmly aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047 aspirations,” while cautioning that the recovery was not yet broad-based.The scale of the increase is evident from the addition to announced project costs. These rose by Rs 46.4 lakh crore over the past two years, compared with just Rs 7 lakh crore added in the eight years up to March 2022. The overall pipeline is now 4.1 times its March 2014 level.IT-enabled services (ITES) and conventional power were the biggest contributors to the latest annual rise, together accounting for 87% of the net increase. ITES added Rs 16.8 lakh crore to the pipeline, while conventional power contributed Rs 7.6 lakh crore.The ITES pipeline alone jumped from Rs 2.2 lakh crore to Rs 18.9 lakh crore in a year, covering 160 projects.Looking at the outstanding pipeline, manufacturing and electricity together made up 74% of the total. Manufacturing projects accounted for Rs 41.3 lakh crore, while electricity projects stood at Rs 32.2 lakh crore.The services sector recorded the highest annual growth rate, surging 347% to Rs 21.9 lakh crore.Maharashtra continued to lead as a destination for announced private investments, with projects worth Rs 28.6 lakh crore. This represented around 29% of the total pipeline.The concentration was also visible in the distribution of fresh additions. Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh together accounted for 94% of the pipeline’s annual increase.UBI Research flagged this concentration, along with the disparity between the growth in announced project costs and the number of projects, as risks for the next phase of the investment cycle.The report also highlighted a substantial difference between planned investments in power generation and transmission. While planned generation investment stood at Rs 32 lakh crore, transmission investment amounted to just Rs 0.17 lakh crore.The pipeline creates significant opportunities for lenders, but the scale of announced investments alone may not be enough to assess the projects. UBI Research called for banks to examine execution prospects, financing requirements and power evacuation arrangements carefully before sanctioning loans.The report’s findings point to a growing pool of planned private investment, but also underline the need to assess whether projects can be executed and supported by the necessary infrastructure.
Article Summary: The pipeline has grown 87% in two years, but the number of projects has increased by only 18%. This suggests that larger projects, rather than a broad increase in investment activity, have accounted for much of the growth. The overall pipeline is now 4.1 times its March 2014 level.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Chennai, schools shut in 4 districts
Article Text:
Heavy rain affected Chennai and nearby areas, prompting school closures as a precautionary measure.

The Regional Meteorological Centre reported significant rainfall across the city and adjoining districts.





CHENNAI: Heavy rain lashed Chennai and neighbouring districts overnight, prompting authorities to declare a holiday for schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu on Wednesday.Chennai collector S Malathi Helen and the collectors of the three neighbouring districts ordered the closures as a precautionary measure amid forecasts of further heavy showers.According to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), weather stations at Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. Several parts of the city, including Taramani, Villivakkam and Nandanam, also received moderate to heavy showers.A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. The wet spell is expected to continue until Oct 26, while another low-pressure area may form over the Bay of Bengal around Oct 23.Meanwhile, the early-morning holiday announcement caught some government school kitchens off guard.Staff had begun preparing breakfast for students in Classes 1 to 8 under the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme before the closure order was issued.“The holiday was declared only around 6am. We started preparing breakfast around 5.30am. We are looking to distribute it to conservancy workers,” a headmaster said.District authorities said any decision on Thursday's closure would depend on the intensity of rainfall and a review of weather conditions on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu closed as a precautionary measure. Weather stations recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs by 2026-end as AI takes on bigger role in bank's operations
Article Text:
Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs

Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year as the British lender streamlines its operations and increases its investment in technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions, including developers, while operational and functional roles will account for most of the job losses.The move comes as Barclays approaches the end of a three-year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking business. Its investment banking division is also affected.In its third-quarter earnings presentation on Thursday, the bank said it was “structurally reducing the cost base to generate capacity for investment.” It described the expected outcome as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.”Barclays said AI was the "icing on the cake" of its wider modernisation strategy. Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts reflected significant investment in technology to simplify and improve the business.Barclays reported pre-tax profit of £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion) for the three months to September, up 12% from the same period a year earlier. The figure matched forecasts compiled by LSEG, although the results were also described as slightly below forecast.Group income stood at £7.4 billion, below analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion, while net interest income was broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion.The bank's CET1 capital ratio, a measure of financial solvency, edged down to 14.2% from 14.3% at the end of the second quarter. Return on tangible equity fell to 11.7% from 16.1%.Barclays shares were almost 1% lower less than an hour into the trading session. Economists are examining company results for evidence that spending on new technology, particularly AI, is improving day-to-day operations, boosting efficiency and reducing staffing requirements.Barclays' latest workforce reduction comes amid this wider scrutiny of how companies are using AI and whether the technology is delivering operational gains.
Article Summary: Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year. The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions.

Article Title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion, but legal charge hits operating income
Article Text:
Meta's Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion

Higher spending planned for AI infrastructure

Meta Platforms' net income more than tripled in the third quarter of 2026, rising 264 per cent year-on-year to $9.86 billion, as higher advertising revenue boosted its financial performance. However, a $9.89 billion legal charge pushed operating income down 37 per cent despite a 26 per cent increase in overall revenue.The company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in the same period last year. Net income stood at $2.71 billion a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $3.83 from $1.05.Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26 per cent from a year ago. The number of ad impressions across its family of applications increased 10 per cent, while the average price per advertisement rose 14 per cent year-on-year.Despite the increase in revenue and net income, operating income dropped to $12.99 billion from $20.54 billion in the year-ago quarter. Total costs and expenses climbed 68 per cent to $51.61 billion, reflecting, among other expenses, a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 US state attorneys general to resolve litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.Meta said that excluding this charge, operating income would have been $22.88 billion. Diluted earnings per share would have reached $7.40, rather than the reported $3.83.Meta expects revenue in the fourth quarter to be between $73 billion and $76 billion. It has also revised its full-year 2026 expense outlook upwards to $175-179 billion, taking the legal charge into account.The company has increased its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $135-145 billion, from the previous range of $130-145 billion. The spending is part of its continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and other business priorities.In the chief financial officer's outlook commentary, Meta said, “Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.”The company said its spending on AI models and infrastructure was opening up additional revenue opportunities. However, it expects these investments to take longer to generate returns than its core business.“While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential,” the commentary said.Meta expects its AI investments, improvements in its models and new product launches to support strong overall revenue growth through 2027.The company is still working on its budget and capacity plans for next year as it continues to invest in AI infrastructure and pursue the revenue opportunities it expects these investments to create.
Article Summary: Meta Platforms' Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion. Company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in same period last year. Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26% from a year ago.
